article.title: Hamstring Flexibility Routine
article.population: Older adults addressed by the NIA 2018 educational guide
article.context: Source-scoped flexibility education; not a soreness or readiness intervention
article.definition: A floor back-of-leg stretch from NIA printed page 82, shown as three ten-second holds for each side.

claims.text: The source gives ten-to-thirty-second holds and three-to-five repetitions for each side. This template represents the lower bounds; unspecified warm-up, relaxation and transition time remain unknown.

limitations: Historical March 2018 guidance for older adults; suitability for an individual is not established.
No improvement in soreness, endurance or strength is claimed from these flexibility instructions.
The source range is 10–30 seconds per hold and 3–5 repeats per side; timer templates use its lower bounds, not a personalized optimum.
Warm-up, repositioning and relaxation durations are unspecified and not counted as zero or estimated automatically.
Source verification and machine validation; no independent human or clinical review.
contraindications: Warm up before stretching; if only stretching, the source suggests a few minutes of easy walking without an exact duration.
Stop for sharp, stabbing or joint pain. Use slow movement without bouncing and breathe normally.
Seek qualified advice when unsure of suitability, particularly following hip or back surgery.

routine.title: Hamstring Flexibility Routine

steps.title: Right back-of-leg hold 1
steps.intensityCue: A mild stretch only; breathe normally. Ten seconds is the lower source bound, not your prescribed target.
steps.techniqueCue: Lie on the back with the opposite knee bent and that foot on the floor. Keep the head and shoulders on the floor. Raise the right leg with its knee slightly bent; grasp that leg with both hands and gently draw it toward the body until a mild back-of-leg stretch is felt. Return slowly to the starting position and relax before the next hold; the relaxation time is not specified.
stopSignals: Sharp, stabbing or joint pain.
Feeling unwell or unable to maintain the source position.

routine.title: Calf Flexibility Routine

steps.title: Left calf hold 1
steps.intensityCue: A mild stretch only; breathe normally. Ten seconds is the lower source bound, not your prescribed target.
steps.techniqueCue: Face a wall slightly beyond arm’s length, feet shoulder-width apart. Place palms on the wall at shoulder height and shoulder-width apart. Step the right foot forward and bend its knee; keep both feet on the floor and slightly bend the left knee until a mild left-calf stretch is felt. Return slowly to the starting position and relax before the next hold; the relaxation time is not specified.
stopSignals: Sharp, stabbing or joint pain.
Feeling unwell or unable to maintain the source position.
